name: Four-View Hologram Compositor
definition: A rendering technique that projects four synchronized views of a 3D scene onto a four-sided acrylic pyramid to create a floating volumetric image. It uses four virtual cameras positioned 90 degrees apart, renders each view to a separate render target, and composites them onto the screen using textured quads with specific rotations and mirrors to match the physical reflection parity of the pyramid.
summary: The Four-View Hologram Compositor renders four synchronized perspective views onto a screen to project a floating volumetric image via a pyramid, distinguishing itself by using physical reflection parity instead of angular sampling.
